resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported. MGS-3 (Master Gas System phase 3, which includes the EWPS-8 to EWPS-10 line) is scheduled to raise network capacity by an additional 3.15 bscfd and to complete by Q4 2028; construction began Q2 2024. Saudi Press Agency official release (N2131194) and Oil & Gas Journal both cite 2028 completion and are independent origins. Broke free of the DEAD_LINK aramco.com press-release ref (that URL times out); SPA carries the same official announcement.

VALUE CONTRADICTION — no source corroborates LengthKnown=190 km for the EWPS-8 to EWPS-10 line '3'. MEED (Package 8, the EWPS-8 to EWPS-10 package) states 'laying 56-inch east-west gas pipelines three and four from EWPS-8 to EWPS-10, covering 480km' — i.e. 480 km for the two parallel lines (three AND four) combined, implying ~240 km per single line, not 190. Independently, L&T reported completing a 120-km stretch of 56-inch pipe within Package 8 (a portion only). GEM's 190 km could not be sourced; recommend reviewing against ~240 km/line. Cited MEED as the ref documenting this segment's length; tier low because the figure does not match the stated value.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported. World Oil explicitly describes 'the third expansion phase of the Master Gas System Network (MGS-3) in Saudi Arabia'; the EWPS-8 to EWPS-10 segment lies entirely within the kingdom's east-west corridor (Eastern Province toward the central/western network). SPA (official) corroborates. Two independent origins.

Owner1=Aramco 100% supported. World Oil reports the EPC letters of intent were issued 'from Saudi Aramco' for the MGS-3 work; SPA's official release announces Aramco awarding the MGS-3 contracts as the project owner/developer. Aramco is the sole owner/operator of the Master Gas System. Two independent origins.
